targetText: The thesis must clearly point out that real freedom for women is possible only through communism. The inseparable connection between the social and human position of the woman, and private property in the means of production, must be strongly brought out. That will draw a clear and ineradicable line of distinction between our policy and feminism.
summary: True women's liberation requires abolishing private ownership of the means of production, distinguishing Marxism from bourgeois feminism.
explanation: While bourgeois feminism seeks equal rights within the existing capitalist hierarchy, Marxism proves that women's oppression is structurally rooted in private property and class exploitation.

targetText: No special organisations for women. A woman communist is a member of the Party just as a man communist, with equal rights and duties. There can be no difference of opinion on that score. Nevertheless, we must not close our eyes to the fact that the Party must have bodies, working groups, commissions, committees, bureaus or whatever you like, whose particular duty it is to arouse the masses of women workers
summary: Equal membership in a single Communist Party combined with specialized Party women's commissions for mass agitation.
explanation: Lenin balances organizational unity (men and women fighting together in one vanguard party) with practical revolutionary reality (dedicated women's bureaus like the Soviet Zhenotdel to organize working women).

targetText: The rejection of the necessity for separate bodies for our work among the women masses is a conception allied to those of our highly principled and most radical friends of the Communist Labour Party. According to them there must be only one form of organisation, workers' unions. I know them. Many revolutionary but confused minds appeal to principle 'whenever ideas are lacking'.
summary: Lenin critiques the ultra-left Communist Labour Party for appealing to abstract 'pure principle' to reject practical organizational work among women.
explanation: Ultra-left sectarians in the German Communist Labour Party (KAPD) opposed dedicated Party women's commissions in the name of abstract organizational purity, ignoring the concrete material obstacles keeping working women from political life.

targetText: Unless millions of women are with us we cannot exercise the proletarian dictatorship, cannot construct on communist lines. We must find our way to them, we must study and try to find that way.
summary: Socialist construction and working-class state power are impossible without the active participation of millions of working women.
explanation: Lenin rebukes sectarian purists who oppose dedicated outreach to women, emphasizing that no mass revolutionary transformation can succeed without mobilizing half the working population.
